entries.title: RHS-IA Documentation
entries.text: RHS-IA is an integrated development environment for data analysis and scientific computing. This guide is bundled with the application and remains available without an internet connection.

entries.title: Getting Started
entries.text: RHS-IA combines an editor, terminal, source control, language runtimes, and data-science tools in one workspace. Open a folder for an existing project, or use File > New Folder to begin from a template.

entries.title: Getting Started
entries.text: Install or select a Python or R interpreter, open a source file, and run code with the editor’s Run action. Output appears in the Console; objects, plots, and data open in their dedicated views. Use View > Command Palette whenever you know an action but not its location. Open this guide from the Documentation icon in the Auxiliary Bar or with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H.

entries.title: Getting Started
entries.text: Learn the workspace layout, configure keyboard shortcuts, or follow a tutorial.

entries.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
entries.text: Open Keyboard Shortcuts from the Command Palette to search actions, inspect conflicts, and change bindings. Select the edit icon beside a command, enter the new key combination, and press Enter. RHS-IA inherits familiar editor shortcuts and adds data-science actions. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P opens the Command Palette, Cmd/Ctrl+` toggles the terminal, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H opens Documentation. On macOS, Cmd commonly replaces Ctrl. Changes are stored in your user keybindings. Use the context-menu reset action to restore a command’s default. Open Keyboard Shortcuts.

entries.title: Command-Line Launcher
entries.text: The command-line launcher opens files and folders in RHS-IA from a terminal. In RHS-IA, open the Command Palette and run Shell Command: Install ‘rhs-ia’ command in PATH when that command is available for your platform. After installation, run rhs-ia . to open the current folder or rhs-ia path/to/file to open a file. Restart the terminal if it was already open so it receives the updated PATH. If the launcher command is unavailable, start RHS-IA normally and use File > Open Folder.

entries.title: Git
entries.text: RHS-IA includes Git source-control integration. Install Git on the computer, open a repository folder, and select Source Control from the Activity Bar. Changed files appear by repository. Select a file to review its diff, stage selected changes with the plus action, enter a commit message, and choose Commit. Fetch, pull, push, branch, clone, and repository initialization actions are available from the Source Control menu and Command Palette. RHS-IA uses the Git identity and credentials configured on your system. Confirm the active branch and staged files before committing.

entries.title: Extensions
entries.text: Extensions add languages, themes, debuggers, and workflow tools. Open Extensions from the Activity Bar to inspect installed extensions or search the configured extension marketplace. Review an extension’s publisher, permissions, settings, and workspace compatibility before installing it. Use the extension’s gear menu to disable, update, or uninstall it. Some changes require Developer: Reload Window. RHS-IA already bundles core data-science functionality; avoid installing another extension that provides the same runtime integration unless its documentation says they are compatible. Open Extensions.

entries.title: Workspace Layout
entries.text: The editor occupies the center of the window. The Primary Side Bar holds Explorer, Search, Source Control, Run and Debug, and Extensions. Panels such as Console and Terminal normally appear below the editor. The Auxiliary Bar holds data-science views and Documentation. Drag view headers to rearrange them, or use View > Appearance and the layout controls to show, hide, and reposition workbench parts. Open a view by name from View: Open View. RHS-IA remembers layout changes per workspace. Use the layout reset action from the Command Palette if a view becomes difficult to locate.

entries.title: Command Palette
entries.text: The Command Palette provides searchable access to RHS-IA actions. Open it with View > Command Palette or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P, type part of an action name, and press Enter. Results change with context: the active editor, selected runtime, and focused view can expose different commands. The gear icon beside a result opens its keyboard-shortcut entry. Quick Open uses the same control for other searches. Remove the leading > to find workspace files, or use the displayed prefixes to search symbols and other targets. Open Settings.

entries.title: Action Bars
entries.text: Action bars place the most relevant controls near the content they affect. Editor actions appear near the editor title, while view actions appear in the view header. Additional actions are grouped under the ellipsis menu. Hover over an icon to read its label and keyboard shortcut. Available actions depend on the file type, language runtime, selection, and view state. If space is limited, RHS-IA moves actions into an overflow menu. The same operation is usually searchable in the Command Palette.

entries.title: Documentation and Language Help
entries.text: RHS-IA separates product documentation from contextual language reference material. Open RHS-IA Documentation from the Auxiliary Bar, the Help menu, or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H. Pages and images are bundled with RHS-IA, so this guide remains usable offline. External HTTPS references open in your default browser. R and Python help requests open the separate Language Help view when supported by the active runtime. That view is hidden until a language-help action requests it; it is not the product documentation home. Documentation follows the RHS-IA display language. Change the application display language and restart RHS-IA to read the documentation in that language.

entries.title: Language Guides
entries.text: RHS-IA provides integrated runtimes for Python and R. A runtime powers code execution, completion, diagnostics, variables, plots, data exploration, and language help. Select an interpreter before running code. The active runtime is shown in the workbench and can be changed with the interpreter-selection commands. Projects may use more than one language, but each console session belongs to a specific runtime. Keep project dependencies in a dedicated environment and record them with the tools customary for that language.

entries.title: Python
entries.text: Open a .py file and choose a discovered Python interpreter. Run a line or selection from the editor to start a Python session and send code to the Console. RHS-IA provides completion, diagnostics, formatting, debugging, variables, plots, and Data Explorer integration through its Python tooling. Notebook kernels use the environment selected for the notebook. Prefer a project-specific virtual environment. Install packages into the same environment used by the active session, then restart the session when native libraries or environment variables change. See Python Installations.

entries.title: R
entries.text: Open an .R file and select an R installation. Run a line or selection from the editor to start an R session and send code to the Console. RHS-IA integrates completion, diagnostics, formatting, debugging, language help, variables, plots, package management, and Data Explorer support. Quarto documents can execute R cells with the selected runtime. Use a project library when reproducibility matters. After changing startup files, library paths, or environment variables, restart R so the session receives the new configuration. See R Installations.

entries.title: Debugging R
entries.text: Set a breakpoint by selecting the gutter beside an executable R line, then start debugging with the R debug action or an applicable Run and Debug configuration. Execution pauses at breakpoints so you can inspect variables, the call stack, and expressions. Use Step Over to run the current line, Step Into to enter a called function, Step Out to finish the current function, and Continue to reach the next breakpoint. Stop ends the debug session. Code evaluated dynamically may not map cleanly to source breakpoints. Save the file and verify that the active R session is using the expected project and function definition.

entries.title: R Session Hooks
entries.text: R startup files and environment files can customize an R session. Common files include project or user .Rprofile and .Renviron files. R determines their precedence and reads them during startup. Keep startup code fast, non-interactive, and safe to run in every session. Avoid storing secrets in files committed to source control. Restart R after changing a startup file. If startup code prevents a session from launching, temporarily rename the project startup file and inspect the R runtime log before restoring changes.

entries.title: Air for R
entries.text: RHS-IA includes Air-based R language tooling when the bundled extension is enabled. It provides editor features such as diagnostics and formatting without requiring an active R console for every operation. Use Format Document or format-on-save settings to apply the configured style. Diagnostics appear in the editor and Problems view. Workspace settings can override user settings for a project. If results differ from the running R session, confirm that both tools use the intended project files and library context, then review the R and extension logs.

entries.title: Data Explorer
entries.text: Data Explorer opens tabular objects in an interactive viewer. Use an object’s Open in Data Explorer action from Variables, a notebook result, or another supported surface. The viewer combines a data grid, filter bar, and summary panel. Sorting and filtering change the view of the data; they do not silently rewrite the runtime object. Large or remote data may be loaded in pages. Available operations and type summaries depend on the language runtime and its data-explorer provider.

entries.title: Data Explorer Grid
entries.text: The data grid displays rows and columns with headers, type indicators, and missing-value representations. Scroll to request additional visible data and resize columns by dragging header boundaries. Select a column header to access supported sorting and filtering operations. Copying a selection places its displayed values on the clipboard. The grid is an inspection surface. Perform durable transformations in Python or R code so they remain reproducible, then reopen or refresh the object to inspect the result.

entries.title: Data Explorer Filter Bar
entries.text: The filter bar narrows the displayed rows without changing the source object. Add a filter, choose a column and condition, and enter the comparison value. Multiple active filters are combined by the viewer. Conditions vary by data type. Text, numeric, logical, date, and missing values expose different operations. Invalid values are reported before a filter is applied. Disable or remove a filter to restore rows. Translate important exploratory filters into source code before sharing or rerunning an analysis.

entries.title: Data Explorer Summary Panel
entries.text: The summary panel describes the selected column. Depending on its type, the panel can show counts, missing values, ranges, distributions, frequencies, or other statistics supplied by the runtime. Select another column to update the summary. Results can be approximate or limited when the provider avoids transferring an entire large data set. Use the panel to spot quality issues and unusual distributions, then calculate and record definitive statistics in project code.

entries.title: Variables
entries.text: The Variables view shows objects in the active runtime session. Entries include a name, type, and compact representation when the runtime can provide one. Expand supported objects to inspect their children. Use contextual actions to view tabular data, copy values, or remove objects when available. The view updates as code creates and changes variables. Switching sessions changes the displayed environment. Treat the view as a live inspection tool; source code, not the session object list, is the reproducible record of an analysis.

entries.title: Plots
entries.text: Plots produced by a supported Python or R runtime appear in the Plots view. Use the history controls to move among plots created in the current session. Resize the view to redraw responsive plots. Available actions can include zoom, open in a larger editor, copy, and export; exact formats depend on the plot provider. For repeatable output, create and save figures from source code with explicit dimensions and file formats. Session plot history is temporary and ends with the runtime session.

entries.title: Database Connections
entries.text: The Connections view represents data sources registered by a supported runtime or extension. Expand a connection to browse catalogs, schemas, tables, and fields supplied by its provider. Connection actions can open objects, preview data, refresh metadata, or disconnect. Credentials and drivers remain the responsibility of the database client or provider; do not place secrets directly in project files. Close unused connections and use read-only credentials when exploration does not require writes. See Connection Extensions for provider integration.

entries.title: Connection Extensions
entries.text: Database and data-source extensions can contribute connection providers to RHS-IA. A provider defines how a connection is registered, browsed, refreshed, and closed. Install a provider only from a trusted publisher and follow its driver and credential setup. Provider behavior may depend on an active Python or R runtime. Extension authors should expose metadata lazily, avoid logging secrets, and dispose connections when a session ends. General development guidance is in Extension Development.

entries.title: Catalog Explorer
entries.text: Catalog Explorer browses supported catalog-backed data sources. Use its tree to navigate namespaces and inspect tables, views, and fields without manually entering every identifier. Refresh the relevant node after external schema changes. Opening or previewing data uses the capabilities and permissions of the configured catalog connection. Metadata visibility does not imply write access. Confirm the selected catalog, namespace, and account before running generated or copied queries.

entries.title: Quarto
entries.text: RHS-IA recognizes Quarto documents and projects, including executable Python and R code cells. Open a .qmd file to edit source, run supported cells, preview equations, and use Quarto-aware editor actions. Rendering requires a compatible Quarto installation and any runtimes used by the document. Run a render action from the editor or terminal; output and errors appear in the associated channel or terminal. Keep document options in YAML frontmatter or project configuration. Use inline output for rapid exploration and a full render to validate the final document.

entries.title: Quarto Inline Output
entries.text: Executable Quarto cells can show results next to their source. Use the cell toolbar to run one cell or an applicable sequence. Text, tables, images, and supported interactive results appear in output zones. Inline results belong to the current runtime session and are not a substitute for the rendered document. Clear output when it is stale, restart the runtime when state matters, and render from a clean session before publication. If a cell is not detected, verify its fenced-code syntax and language identifier.

entries.title: Jupyter Notebooks
entries.text: Open an .ipynb file to edit Markdown and executable code cells. Select a kernel that matches the notebook language and environment, then run individual cells or the entire notebook. Execution order matters because a notebook kernel keeps state. Restart the kernel and run all cells before relying on a result or sharing the file. Saved cell output can differ from the current kernel state. RHS-IA includes a data-science notebook editor and the legacy editor for compatibility.

entries.title: Notebook Editor
entries.text: The RHS-IA notebook editor integrates notebook cells with language runtimes, Variables, Plots, and Data Explorer. Use cell toolbars to run, stop, move, add, or delete cells and the notebook toolbar for document-wide actions. Choose the kernel before execution. Code-cell status shows whether a cell is queued, running, completed, or failed. Interrupt stops current execution; restart clears kernel state. Use Markdown cells for explanation and keep code cells focused so the notebook remains understandable when run from top to bottom.

entries.title: Legacy Notebook Editor
entries.text: The legacy notebook editor preserves the standard editor workflow used by compatible extensions and existing workspaces. It supports kernel selection, cell editing, execution, output, and notebook commands. Use Reopen Editor With from the editor tab context menu when more than one notebook editor is registered. The selection can be applied once or remembered for the file type. Changing editors does not change the notebook file format, but unsaved edits and active kernel state should be handled before switching.

entries.title: Code Cells
entries.text: Code cells contain executable source associated with a notebook kernel or Quarto runtime. Run the active cell from its toolbar or keyboard shortcut; use run-above and run-below actions when execution order is important. A cell can produce text, structured data, plots, errors, or interactive output. Trust notebook output only from known sources, and clear sensitive results before sharing a file. After changing dependencies or global state, restart the kernel and run all cells to confirm that the document is reproducible.

entries.title: Developing Data Applications
entries.text: RHS-IA can run supported data applications from project files and display them in the Viewer or an external browser. Available run actions depend on the language, framework, and installed packages. Select the correct runtime, open the application’s entry file, and use its Run App action. Stop or restart the running task after changing startup configuration or dependencies. Keep application configuration and reproducible launch instructions in the project. Bind development servers only to trusted interfaces, and never commit credentials used by the application.

entries.title: Folder Templates
entries.text: Use File > New Folder to create a workspace from an available template. Templates can prepare a basic project, Python or R workspace, notebook, or other supported structure. Choose a template, destination, and folder name, then review the files and initialization actions before creation. Some templates can initialize source control or create language-specific files. Open the generated folder as a workspace and select its interpreter. A template is a starting point; inspect generated configuration before adding credentials or production data.

entries.title: Remote SSH
entries.text: Remote SSH opens a folder on an SSH host while the RHS-IA interface remains local. Configure the host in your SSH configuration, then run a Remote SSH connect action and choose the destination. Extensions and runtimes needed by the remote workspace may run on the host. Paths, terminals, ports, and interpreter discovery therefore reflect the remote system. Use key-based authentication and verify a host key before accepting it. If connection fails, test the same host with the system SSH client and inspect the Remote SSH log.

entries.title: Development Containers
entries.text: Development containers provide a project-specific toolchain defined by container configuration. With a compatible container engine available, use a Dev Containers action to reopen or build the workspace in its container. The first build may take time because images and dependencies must be prepared. Terminals, extensions, and language runtimes can run inside the container while the interface remains local. Review container definitions before building them. Rebuild after changing the image or setup commands, and keep persistent data in mounted workspace or volume locations.

entries.title: Managing Interpreters
entries.text: An interpreter identifies the Python or R installation used to start a runtime. Use the interpreter selector or Command Palette to view discovered installations and select one for the workspace. RHS-IA remembers suitable selections in workspace state. A newly created virtual environment or newly installed runtime may require a refresh or window reload before it appears. Choose project-local environments when possible, verify the displayed executable path, and restart active sessions after changing interpreters. Continue with Python Installations or R Installations.

entries.title: Interpreter Startup
entries.text: RHS-IA can start a runtime when code execution or another language feature needs it. Startup uses the selected interpreter, workspace directory, environment variables, and language-specific initialization files. The Console reports startup progress and errors. If a runtime does not start, confirm the executable still exists, test it in a terminal, and inspect the relevant output channel. Then select the interpreter again or restart the window. Startup code should not request interactive terminal input because the language session may initialize before a console prompt is available.

entries.title: Package Management
entries.text: The Packages view displays packages for the active Python or R runtime and exposes supported install, update, remove, and load actions. Package operations run against the environment owned by that session. Confirm the active interpreter before changing packages. For reproducible projects, use a project environment and the language’s dependency lock or requirements file instead of relying only on the global library. Restart the runtime if an installed package is not immediately importable, especially after changes to compiled dependencies or library paths.

entries.title: Python Installations
entries.text: RHS-IA discovers system Python installations and common virtual and environment-manager environments. The selected executable determines the runtime and package set for Python files. Create environments with your preferred Python tool, then use the interpreter selector to choose the resulting executable. On macOS and Linux this is commonly under bin/python; on Windows it is commonly under Scripts or the environment root. Avoid modifying the operating system’s managed Python. A project-local environment reduces dependency conflicts and makes the selected interpreter easier to identify.

entries.title: R Installations
entries.text: RHS-IA discovers supported R installations available on the computer. Select an installation for the workspace before starting an R session. The chosen R executable, startup files, library paths, and environment determine the packages visible to the session. Use a project library or dependency manager when the project must be reproducible. After installing a different R version, refresh interpreter discovery or reload the window. If startup fails, run the executable in a terminal and inspect the R output channel for missing libraries or startup-file errors.

entries.title: Reticulate
entries.text: Reticulate lets an R session call Python. The Python environment selected by reticulate is separate from the Python runtime that RHS-IA may use for standalone Python files. Configure the reticulate Python environment before importing Python modules in R. Once Python has initialized inside the R process, changing environments generally requires restarting R. When troubleshooting, compare the executable reported by reticulate with the environment you intended to use and confirm that required Python packages are installed there.

entries.title: Environment Modules
entries.text: On systems that provide environment modules, RHS-IA can use module-managed tools and runtimes when the environment-modules integration is enabled and configured. Load the required module set before selecting an interpreter or launching related tools. A module change can alter PATH, library paths, and other environment variables, so restart affected runtime sessions afterward. Available modules are controlled by the host system. If a module or interpreter is missing, verify the same module command in a login shell and consult the site’s module configuration.

entries.title: Extension Development
entries.text: RHS-IA supports extensions built for its compatible extension API. Start with an extension project, declare contributions and activation behavior in package.json, and implement the extension host entry point. Press F5 from an extension workspace to launch an Extension Development Host. Use the extension host log, developer tools, and automated tests to diagnose activation and contribution problems. Use only APIs present in the RHS-IA build you target. Package the extension as a VSIX for local installation, and test it in a clean profile before distribution.

entries.title: Tutorials
entries.text: The tutorials exercise the core RHS-IA workflow with small local projects. Choose the Jupyter Notebook tutorial for an interactive cell-based analysis or the Quarto tutorial for an executable document. Before starting, install a supported Python or R interpreter and the packages required by your chosen example. Work in a new folder so generated files and environment configuration remain isolated. Each tutorial ends with a clean-session check to make sure the result can be reproduced.

entries.title: Jupyter Notebook Tutorial
entries.text: Create a folder and open it in RHS-IA. Create an .ipynb notebook and choose a Python or R kernel. Add a Markdown cell that describes the analysis. Add a code cell that creates a small table, then run it. Open the table in Data Explorer and create a plot in another cell. Restart the kernel and run all cells. Save the notebook after the clean run. If a cell fails, verify the selected kernel and install the missing package into that kernel’s environment.

entries.title: Quarto Tutorial
entries.text: Create a folder and a .qmd file with a title in YAML frontmatter. Add explanatory Markdown and a fenced Python or R code cell. Select the matching interpreter and run the cell inline. Add a calculation or plot that depends on the first cell. Render the document with Quarto and inspect the output. Finally, restart the runtime and render again. A successful clean render confirms that the document does not depend on hidden interactive state.

entries.title: Troubleshooting
entries.text: Start by reproducing the problem in the smallest relevant workspace. Note the active interpreter, remote context, file type, and exact action that failed. Open View > Output and choose the related channel. Runtime startup failures usually require checking the executable and startup files; extension failures may require Developer: Show Running Extensions or an Extension Host log. Use Developer: Reload Window after configuration or extension changes. If the issue persists, record RHS-IA and operating-system versions, concise reproduction steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, and sanitized log excerpts. Never include credentials or sensitive data.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.text: No. Product pages, styles, and images are bundled with RHS-IA. Only explicitly selected external HTTPS references use your browser.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.text: Confirm that it runs in a terminal, refresh interpreter discovery, and reload the window. Remote workspaces discover interpreters on the remote host.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.section: Where did my variables or plots go?
entries.text: They belong to a runtime session. Select the correct session, or rerun the source after a restart.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.section: How do I reset the interface?
entries.text: Use the layout reset action from the Command Palette, then reopen the required view by name.

entries.title: About RHS-IA
entries.text: RHS-IA is an integrated development environment focused on data analysis and scientific computing. It brings source editing, terminals, source control, Python and R runtimes, notebooks, executable documents, variables, plots, and data exploration into one workbench. This bundled guide documents the RHS-IA software available in the current build. Features supplied by third-party extensions can have separate documentation and support terms. See Documentation Attribution and License for the provenance and reuse terms of this guide.
